Please give me one count per forename, so I can compare the two — if they turn out to be equal, just report both counts side by side. Nothing else needed.
gold_sql: SELECT T1.forename, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.driverId) AS winner_drivers FROM drivers AS T1 INNER JOIN results AS T2 ON T2.driverId = T1.driverId WHERE T2.positionOrder = 1 AND T1.forename IN ('John','Peter') GROUP BY T1.forename ORDER BY T1.forename
pred_sql:
SELECT d.forename, COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) AS winners_count
FROM drivers d
JOIN results r ON d.driverId = r.driverId
WHERE r.positionOrder = 1
AND (d.forename = 'Peter' OR d.forename = 'John')
GROUP BY d.forename;
raw_response: There have been 3 different drivers named Peter who have won a Formula 1 race, and 2 different drivers named John who have won a Formula 1 race.

question: I'm working on a story about qualifying records. Across all races, which driver set the fastest time in Q3 (the final part of qualifying)? I'd like the nationality of that driver - and if more than one driver shares the fastest Q3 time, please give me every such driver's nationality. I don't need anything else, just the nationality or nationalities.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE TRIM(q.q3) = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q3) <> '')

FROM qualifying q
JOIN drivers d ON q.driverId = d.driverId
WHERE q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3 != ''
AND (CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, 1, INSTR(q.q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000 + CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3, INSTR(q.q3, ':') + 1) AS REAL)) =
    (SELECT MIN(CAST(SUBSTR(q3, 1, INSTR(q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000 + CAST(SUBSTR(q3, INSTR(q3, ':') + 1) AS REAL))
     FROM qualifying

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, which driver set the second-fastest time in the second qualifying session (Q2), and which constructor did he drive for that weekend? JOIN drivers d ON q.driverId = d.driverId
JOIN constructors c ON q.constructorId = c.constructorId
WHERE q.raceId = 981

ORDER BY (SELECT grid FROM results WHERE raceId = q.raceId AND driverId = q.driverId) ASC

question: I'm putting together a review of last fall's activities and want to see how the Women's Soccer game compared to a typical event that semester. question: I'm reviewing our roster against the catalog and want to see how much of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences' coverage our members actually hold, department by department. For each department in that college, give me: the department's name, the majors it offers, the majors held by at least one of our members, and the average members per major it offers, rounded to two decimals. Membership is as currently listed in the member records, and count a department as belonging to the college when any of its majors sits in the college.
gold_sql: SELECT m.department, COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id) AS majors_offered, COUNT(DISTINCT mem.link_to_major) AS majors_held, ROUND(1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT mem.member_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id), 2) AS avg_members_per_major FROM major m LEFT JOIN member mem ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id WHERE m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' GROUP BY m.department
pred_sql:
WITH major_members AS (
  SELECT m.department, m.major_name, COUNT(DISTINCT mb.member_id) AS members_per_major
  FROM major m
  LEFT JOIN member mb ON m.major_id = mb.link_to_major
  WHERE m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences'
  GROUP BY m.department, m.major_name
)
SELECT department,
       GROUP_CONCAT(major_name, ', ') AS majors_offered,
       GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN members_per_major > 0 THEN major_name END, ', ') AS majors_held_by_members,
       ROUND(CAST(SUM(members_per_major) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(major_name), 2) AS avg_members_per_major
FROM major_members
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY department;
raw_response: For each department in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, this query lists the department name, the majors it offers, the majors held by at least one member, and the average members per major rounded to two decimals.

question: Our officer team wants to settle a debate about whether we pull more weight than the rest of the club, so we need the attendance numbers before the next meeting. question: I'm wrapping up the October Meeting and need the final numbers broken down by what we actually bought, not just by budget category. For every item bought with approved money for the October Meeting, can you give me: the item's name, the budget category of the purchase that included the item, and the total cost in dollars of the approved October Meeting purchases that included the item? FROM expense e
JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
JOIN event ev ON b.link_to_event = ev.event_id
WHERE ev.event_name = 'October Meeting'
AND e.approved = 'true'
GROUP BY e.expense_description, b.category
ORDER BY b.category, e.expense_description;
raw_response: For the October Meeting, the approved purchases include Posters in Advertisement category costing $54.25, Pizza in Food category costing $51.81, and Water, chips, cookies in Food category costing $69.33.

question: I want to know whether molecular saturation is associated with carcinogenicity in our compound library. Please report, for molecules in which every bond is a single bond: the number of carcinogenic molecules minus the number of non-carcinogenic molecules. And for all other molecules: the same difference (carcinogenic count minus non-carcinogenic count). Rules: label '+' means the molecule is carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic; bond type '-' denotes a single bond; each molecule belongs to exactly one of the two groups.
gold_sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule m WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_molecules_with_only_single_bonds, (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule m WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_other_molecules
pred_sql:
WITH bond_summary AS (
  SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS total_bonds, SUM(CASE WHEN bond_type = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS single_bonds
  FROM bond
  GROUP BY molecule_id
),
molecule_groups AS (
  SELECT molecule_id,
         CASE WHEN total_bonds = single_bonds THEN 'saturated' ELSE 'unsaturated' END AS saturation_status
  FROM bond_summary
),
carcinogenic_counts AS (
  SELECT mg.saturation_status,
         SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS carcinogenic_count,
         SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_carcinogenic_count
  FROM molecule m
  JOIN molecule_groups mg ON m.molecule_id = mg.molecule_id
  GROUP BY mg.saturation_status
)
SELECT saturation_status, carcinogenic_count - non_carcinogenic_count AS difference
FROM carcinogenic_counts;
raw_response: For molecules with only single bonds (saturated), the difference between carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic molecules is 9; for molecules with other bond types (unsaturated), the difference is -48.

  SELECT element, molecule_id
  FROM atom
  GROUP BY element, molecule_id
), ElementCounts AS (
  SELECT element, COUNT(molecule_id) AS molecule_count

  GROUP BY element
